answer: Ping triangulation: each fake needs its own physical host in a distinct city (~$40/month per identity). Every epoch, 5 random verifiers in different regions ping an agent; its RTT terrace, the stepped latency profile across them, must fit one location and match its own history, and a canyon over 3 ms between predicted and measured RTT rejects it. A garden of sybils on one rack shows identical terraces and is merged into one identity. A farm can't share or bulk-rent one box to pass; VPN relays add jitter that fails the fit. Limit: it raises cost, not to infinity.
